mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md (Training and career development section — 'fellowship pairs the research work plan with structured training in the MSCA-PF mandatory transferable dimensions'); strategic_positioning.md (§2.1 Career perspectives / employability — CDP milestones, publications, MSc co-supervision, follow-on proposal)
mappings.mapping_description: The concept explicitly describes structured training in the MSCA-PF mandatory transferable dimensions: digital and AI skills including the responsible use of generative AI in environmental modelling and scientific coding, knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship for translating the uncertainty-aware demonstrator toward user uptake, and research integrity/open-science ethics (FAIR data management, open research software, reproducible validation). The Career Development Plan commits to ≥120 hours of transferable-skills training, ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host, and a follow-on national or ERC-track proposal submitted within six months of the fellowship end — all activities directly addressing improved employability and career prospects within academia and beyond.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md (Consortium and identity — Fellowship type: 'European Fellowship (EF), 24 months (Plovdiv, Bulgaria → ELTE, Hungary; intra-EU)'; Two-way transfer of knowledge section); strategic_positioning.md (§1.3 Supervision, training, two-way transfer of knowledge; §1.4 The researcher's professional experience — 'The Bulgaria → Hungary move satisfies the MSCA mobility rule')
mappings.mapping_description: Inference chain: The concept describes international mobility (Dr. Cholakova, Bulgaria → ELTE, Hungary — intra-EU European Fellowship), a genuinely interdisciplinary pairing (plant physiology fellow × geoinformatics/remote sensing host and supervisor), and engagement with the non-academic associated partner AgroVIR for field validation and farmer access. These three mechanisms constitute the international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience through which new mind-sets and approaches to R&I work are forged per EO-02. The two-way knowledge transfer (plant physiology into geoinformatics; geoinformatics methods back to the fellow) is the explicit mechanism of new approach acquisition. The term 'inter-sectoral' is not used verbatim but AgroVIR's non-academic sector role provides the inter-sectoral dimension. 'New mind-sets' is not stated explicitly but is the logical outcome of the described cross-disciplinary and cross-country mobility.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md (Training and career development — 'A Career Development Plan is prepared jointly by supervisor and fellow and submitted as a project deliverable at the start of the action (by months 2–3), then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24'); strategic_positioning.md (§1.3 — 'Supervision is structured around a Career Development Plan... regular research reviews, and a genuine two-way transfer... ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host')
mappings.mapping_description: Inference chain: The concept describes a Career Development Plan jointly prepared by supervisor (Dr. András Jung) and fellow (Dr. Rositsa Cholakova), submitted as a project deliverable at project start (months 2–3), then reviewed and updated at M12 and M24, supported by regular research reviews and a genuine two-way knowledge transfer (plant physiology expertise into the host group; geoinformatics/remote sensing methods back to the fellow, evidenced by ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host). This structured, milestone-tracked supervisory arrangement constitutes enhanced quality and sustainability of research training and supervision (EO-05). 'Sustainability' in the training context is not used verbatim; the M12/M24 review cycle provides the inference basis for longitudinal sustained quality.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: strategic_positioning.md (§2.1 — '≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author)... follow-on national or ERC-track proposal submitted within six months of the fellowship end'; §2.2 — 'open research software, open validation data and protocol')
mappings.mapping_description: Inference chain: The concept describes ≥3 peer-reviewed publications (≥2 first-author), an open TRL 3–4 research demonstrator (uncertainty-aware crop water stress decision support tool), open research software, open validation data and protocol, and a follow-on ERC-track proposal — all hosted at and attributed to ELTE Budapest. These outputs logically increase ELTE's global attractiveness, visibility and reputation as a research host with emerging capability at the intersection of geoinformatics, probabilistic machine learning and crop science. The terms 'global attractiveness', 'visibility' and 'reputation' do not appear verbatim; the inference is from the described output portfolio.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: concept_note.md (Two-way transfer of knowledge section — 'Two-way transfer of knowledge. The fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise... into the host's geoinformatics group; the host provides geoinformatics, remote-sensing and hyperspectral/multisensor-fusion methods and infrastructure in return'); strategic_positioning.md (§1.3 — '≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host'; §2.1 — ≥3 publications)
mappings.mapping_description: The concept explicitly uses the phrase 'two-way transfer of knowledge': the fellow brings plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise into the host's geoinformatics group; the host provides geoinformatics, remote-sensing and hyperspectral/multisensor-fusion methods and infrastructure in return, evidenced by ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host. R&I output is explicitly evidenced by ≥3 peer-reviewed publications, a TRL 3–4 research demonstrator, and open research software. R&I capacity is explicitly built through the combination of plant physiology (fellow) and geoinformatics/remote sensing (host) competences — a capacity neither organisation held independently before the fellowship.

mappings.tier3_evidence_ref: strategic_positioning.md (§1.3 — '≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host'; §2.1 — 'co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at the host')
mappings.mapping_description: Inference chain: The concept describes co-supervision of ≥1 MSc thesis at ELTE and ≥2 methods seminars delivered at the host institution. These are the specific mechanisms by which research results from the uncertainty-aware crop water stress and irrigation decision-support project feed into teaching and education at ELTE. Co-supervision of an MSc thesis directly embeds project methodology into graduate education. Methods seminars deliver research insights into the host department's educational programme. The term 'regular feedback' is not used verbatim; 'teaching' does not appear explicitly, but co-supervision of MSc theses and departmental seminars are the standard academic mechanisms for research-to-teaching feedback.
